title: Microsoft Copilot: build interactive reports and dashboards with Pages
summary: The roadmap facts and existing Pages controls are supported, and the briefing clearly separates them from the new capability's unconfirmed licensing and governance. One minor correction should acknowledge Microsoft's differing descriptions of access to existing Pages after the creation policy is disabled.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether the new interactive elements depend on the code-preview setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Pages" "interactive reports" dashboards license policy default; "Enable code previews" "Graph" "PowerShell" Copilot Pages. Opened cpcn-admin-configuration; it describes code previews and lightweight apps but not this new capability's dependency.

claims.claim: The Pages creation policy is under Customization > Policy Management > policy configuration > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks in Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: Select Customization from the left pane. ... Select Policy Management. ... Create a new policy configuration or edit an existing one. ... From the Choose the scope dropdown list ... In Configure Settings ... Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks

claims.claim: A Graph beta POST to admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors with application/json and a configurationMonitor containing displayName, mode applyOnce and a baseline applies desired state once.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors
Content-Type: application/json

An active applyOnce monitor runs in the background on behalf of the signed-in administrator and then becomes inactive.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The separate code-preview policy is under the stated Cloud Policy path and controls running previews, including lightweight apps, in Copilot Chat and Pages.
claims.quote: Select Customization ... Select Policy Management ... Choose the scope ... Configure Settings ... Enable code previews for AI-generated content in Microsoft Copilot Chat and Copilot Pages ... Disabled: Copilot doesn't run code previews in Copilot Chat or Copilot Pages.

claims.claim: No automation for the code-preview policy is documented, and the TCM Copilot resource list contains no code-preview resource.
claims.quote: Searched: "Enable code previews" "Graph" "PowerShell" Copilot Pages; "code previews" "Office Cloud Policy" API automation. Opened cpcn-admin-configuration and searched the full utcm-copilot-resources text for code.preview; no resource or automation was documented.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; controls[2].api; controls[2].note; Governance controls table

claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Pages" "interactive reports" dashboards license policy default; "Copilot Pages" "reports and dashboards" settings agents permissions storage. Opened cpcn-admin-configuration and utcm-copilot-resources and read the roadmap; no separate switch appears.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Purview retention policies configured for all SharePoint sites are enforced for Copilot Pages and Notebooks.
claims.quote: Retention policies from Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management configured for all SharePoint sites are enforced for all Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks.

claims.quote: Audit logs: Available for all events. Retained, exportable, and streamable to third-party tools. Search in Purview for "page" and filter by "SourceFileExtension":"page".

claims.claim: Conditional Access applies to the whole Microsoft Copilot app rather than Pages separately.
claims.quote: Conditional Access: Only applies at the app level. Because Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks are features of the Microsoft Copilot app, Conditional Access applies to the entire app at m365.cloud.microsoft.

claims.claim: Information Barriers are not supported for content stored in SharePoint Embedded containers.
claims.quote: Information Barriers are not supported for content stored in SharePoint Embedded containers.

claims.quote: Pages and Notebooks are stored in OneDrive for Business: the same visible file system where Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files live.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Pages created before November 2025 remain in a user-owned SharePoint Embedded container.
claims.quote: Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks created before November 2025 continue to be stored in the user-owned SharePoint Embedded container. These legacy Copilot Pages and legacy Copilot Notebooks haven't moved to OneDrive for Business.

claims.claim: Legacy Pages count against the organisation's SharePoint storage quota.
claims.quote: All legacy Copilot Pages and legacy Copilot Notebooks count against your organization's SharePoint storage quota.

claims.claim: The storage overview says current Pages count against the user's OneDrive storage limit.
claims.quote: | Quota | Counts against user's OneDrive storage limit |

claims.claim: The admin, requirements and compliance pages instead describe Pages as using a user-owned SharePoint Embedded container and the organisation's SharePoint quota.
claims.quote: Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks are stored together in a single user-owned SharePoint Embedded container, which is also shared by Loop My workspace. Storage counts against your organization's SharePoint quota.

claims.claim: Without Loop components enabled, Pages are interactive only in the Microsoft Copilot app and supported chat experiences, not as embedded interactive components in other listed apps.
claims.quote: Without Loop components enabled in the Microsoft 365 ecosystem, Copilot Pages are only interactive within the Microsoft Copilot app and supported chat experiences.

claims.claim: The requirements page lists a OneDrive licence for existing Copilot Pages.
claims.quote: Users need a OneDrive license and an active OneDrive site.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: Existing Copilot Pages require an active OneDrive site.
claims.quote: Users need a OneDrive license and an active OneDrive site.

claims.claim: The requirements page says Pages continue working if the licence is removed after the OneDrive site exists.
claims.quote: If a OneDrive site exists and the license is later removed, Copilot Pages continue to work.

claims.quote: Users need the Microsoft Copilot or Copilot Chat license.

claims.claim: No meter or Copilot Credits rate is documented specifically for Pages as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Pages" "Copilot Credits" meter billing. Opened cpcn-requirements, cpcn-storage and copilot/plan/pay-as-you-go-meters; read requirements-messages-management billing excerpts. Agent billing is documented, but no Pages-specific meter or rate was found.

claims.claim: People whose OneDrive creation is disabled cannot create existing Copilot Pages.
claims.quote: If your organization disabled the creation of OneDrive, regardless of the setting noted here, these people in your organization can't create Copilot Pages or Copilot Notebooks.

claims.claim: An Exchange Online mailbox is required for full functionality including @mentions.
claims.quote: For full functionality including @mentions, users need an Exchange Online mailbox. Users with Exchange On-Premises mailboxes have limited capabilities.

claims.claim: The network requirements include WebSocket traffic to *.svc.ms and *.office.com for real-time collaboration.
claims.quote: Allow WebSocket traffic to *.svc.ms and *.office.com endpoints. WebSocket connections enable real-time collaboration features including live editing, presence indicators, and shared cursors.

claims.claim: Learn documents a two-group Cloud Policy pattern with the enabled pilot group at a lower priority number than the disabled All users group.
claims.quote: Create Group B that includes All users. Assign the same Cloud Policy to this group and set it to Disabled. ... Set the priority for Group A to a lower number (for example, priority 0) so it's evaluated before Group B (for example, priority 1).

claims.claim: Disabling creation does not delete existing Pages.
claims.quote: Existing Copilot Pages and Notebooks aren't deleted.

claims.claim: After creation is disabled, users can still view and edit existing items if they have permission.
claims.quote: Users can still view and edit existing items if they have permission.
claims.fix: After this sentence add: 'The TCM reference gives a narrower Copilot Chat result: "When disabled, Copilot Chat doesn't provide live access to view or edit shared Loop files" (https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-copilot-resources#copilotpagesnotebooks-resource-type).'

claims.claim: Preventing creation of the shared user-owned container requires disabling both the Pages/Notebooks policy and Create Loop workspaces in Loop for the same user.
claims.quote: The shared container is created when either the Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks policy or the Loop Create Loop workspaces in Loop policy allows creation for the user. To prevent the container from being created, disable both policies for the same user.

claims.claim: The Graph TCM operation and Copilot resource support are preview.
claims.quote: This article lists the Copilot resource types supported in preview for monitoring and snapshots through the Tenant Configuration Management (TCM) APIs in Microsoft Graph beta. These resources also support remediation and applyOnce.

claims.claim: TCM supports these settings only in tenant-level policies in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.
claims.quote: TCM supports these settings only in tenant-level policies in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.

claims.claim: The TCM target setting must not be configured in a group-level policy.
claims.quote: Before using TCM, ensure that the target setting isn't configured in any group-level policy in that admin center. If it is, monitoring, snapshots, remediation, and applyOnce fail for that resource.

claims.claim: The calling app needs delegated ConfigurationMonitoring.ReadWrite.All for applyOnce.
claims.quote: Creating an applyOnce monitor supports delegated permissions only. In addition to the calling app's delegated ConfigurationMonitoring.ReadWrite.All permission, the TCM service principal needs delegated permissions for the target workloads

claims.claim: The TCM service principal needs delegated CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite for remediation and applyOnce.
claims.quote: For remediation and applyOnce, grant it the CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite delegated permission.

claims.claim: AI Administrator is the least-privileged signed-in user role for remediation and applyOnce.
claims.quote: AI Administrator is the least-privileged role for the signed-in user for remediation and applyOnce; don't assign that user-role requirement to the service principal.

claims.claim: The baseline resourceType is microsoft.copilot.copilotpagesnotebooks.
claims.quote: "resourceType": "microsoft.copilot.copilotpagesnotebooks"

claims.claim: The baseline resourceVersion is 1.
claims.quote: All resources on this page use resourceVersion: 1 and are singletons.

claims.claim: A string properties.value of "0" disables the Pages/Notebooks policy.
claims.quote: The value property is a string, not a Boolean or a number. ... 0 disables the setting; 1 enables the setting.

claims.claim: A string properties.value of "1" enables the Pages/Notebooks policy.
claims.quote: "properties": { "value": "1" } ... 0 disables the setting; 1 enables the setting.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether the existing Pages prerequisites also apply to the new capability.
